gaps.sentence: 'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
gaps.explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
